name: Emergency Electricity Payment Scheme
shortDescription: Emergency assistance of up to $800 for eligible households with electricity debt who have been disconnected or are at risk of disconnection.
plainEnglishSummary: If you cannot pay your electricity debt and your power has been disconnected or may soon be disconnected, a financial counsellor may be able to assess your situation and apply for an emergency payment on your behalf.
audience: South Australian households experiencing serious financial hardship
Electricity customers with unpaid electricity debt
Households whose electricity has been disconnected
Households at risk of electricity disconnection
supportTypes: Support for households at risk of disconnection
availabilityNote: At the last verification date of 17 August 2026, an eligible household could receive up to $800, not exceeding the value of its eligible electricity debt. The payment is credited directly to the electricity account and is generally available no earlier than two years after the household's previous EEPS payment.
eligibilityNote: Community Connect cannot confirm eligibility. EEPS is intended for households in financial crisis with electricity debt that have been disconnected or are at risk of disconnection. Individuals cannot lodge an application directly; an accredited financial counsellor must assess the household's circumstances and submit the application.
